kind: descriptive comparison of two experimental crystal structures (static); no ensemble, population, kinetic or functional inference
question: Where along the KRAS backbone does local Calpha geometry differ between GDP-bound (9O0N) and GMPPNP-bound (9O0O) wild-type KRAS(1-169), both crystallized with MRTX1133, and do curvature/torsion, window-matched Calpha distances and proper-rotation local Calpha RMSD locate the same differences?

selection.screen: RCSB search: UniProt P01116, X-ray, GNP- or GDP-bound (111 and 320 entries); pairs with identical entity sequence and one polymer entity within one primary citation; full non-polymer entity lists checked

examined_pairs.B: 9U5T (GDP) / 9USB (GMPPNP), wild type with a pan-KRAS inhibitor in both: not usable here because RCSB provides mmCIF only and no mmCIF reader is available in the existing environments (MDAnalysis without gemmi); no installation in scope

selection.identified_not_examined: 5US4 (GDP) / 5USJ (GMPPNP), KRAS G12D, Welsch et al. Cell 2017: the only matched pair in the screen without a pharmacological ligand; not examined because of the two-pair limit
selection.reason: matched construct (identical sequence, residues 0-169 incl. expression-tag Gly0), wild type, one chain each, high resolution, same inhibitor in both, primary paper documents the context

GNP.observed_residues: 0-168 (Lys169 unobserved); side chain of Asp30 incomplete (REMARK 470)

access: PDB archive data CC0 1.0 (wwPDB policy, as recorded in docs/C1_FEASIBILITY_CHECKS_2026-10-13.md); primary citation Bonsor et al., Nat Commun 17:1614 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41467-026-68319-1, CC BY
independent_context: The authors report that the two structures superimpose with a low RMSD (0.3 A) and show minor differences in Switch-I and -II, that MRTX1133 occupies the Switch-II pocket, and (ITC) that MRTX1133 binds wild-type KRAS in both nucleotide states with tighter binding to the GDP-bound state (PMC12905138, Results). The two crystals grew in different conditions (Methods).

mapping.residues: 1-168 (author numbering, no insertion codes), explicit correspondence list; residue names must match between structures

altloc.sensitivity: highest_occupancy (reported as unavailable if the adapter rejects a tie)

windows.three_residue: centered on residue i: (i-1, i, i+1)
windows.four_residue: (i-1, i, i+1, i+2), hinge i -> i+1

metrics.d_kappa: |kappa_GNP - kappa_GDP| (rad), three-residue window, from the TopoFold core
metrics.d_tau: circular |wrap(tau_GNP - tau_GDP)| (rad), four-residue window, from the TopoFold core
metrics.rmsd3: proper-rotation Calpha RMSD of the three-residue window after optimal superposition (MDAnalysis QCP, MDAnalysis.analysis.rms.rmsd with center and superposition) (A)
metrics.rmsd4: the same for the four-residue window (A)
metrics.global_rmsd: Calpha RMSD over all mapped residues after optimal superposition (MDAnalysis QCP), context only

equal_information: every metric uses the same mapped Calpha coordinates (adapter output) for the same residues
reporting: residue-mapped table of all metrics; windows touching an altloc residue flagged
per metric: the ten largest windows (descriptive)
Spearman rank correlation between metrics on shared windows (descriptive)
global RMSD beside the authors' reported value (context only)
altloc sensitivity: maximum change of each metric
permitted_interpretation: Direct geometric differences between these two crystal structures. Confounded by crystal form and packing (different space groups and crystallization conditions), resolution (1.40 vs 1.90 A), alternate conformations and coordinate error; both contain MRTX1133, so this is not apo KRAS. No ensemble, population, kinetic or functional-state claim; nucleotide identity does not establish functional state; agreement or disagreement between metrics does not show that one representation is better.
